key_insight: A staged text-to-FHIR pipeline can turn unstructured case text into clinically realistic, interoperable EHR data for more deployment-aligned evaluation of LLM diagnostic reasoning.
clinical_relevance: Structured FHIR-style inputs better reflect real clinical systems, and this benchmark shows LLM diagnostic performance can drop when moving from plain text to realistic EHR-congruent data.
method: Generated HL7 FHIR R4 bundles from unstructured clinical text using staged LLM synthesis.
Applied terminology-grounded validation and repair to reduce hallucinated codes and improve structural and semantic consistency.
Built MedCase-Structured from MedCaseReasoning for synthetic, clinician-aligned diagnostic cases.
evidence_signal: The pipeline achieved valid FHIR generation for 82.5% of cases, and evaluation found lower diagnostic accuracy on structured FHIR inputs than on plain text.
watch_item: Synthetic FHIR generation still depends on validation quality and may not capture all complexities of real-world EHR data.
paper_title: MedCase-Structured: A Text-to-FHIR Dataset for Benchmarking Diagnostic Reasoning in Clinically Realistic EHR Settings
